records.issue_text: `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:6-10` uses computed property keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]`. Since Zod schema objects don't override `toString()`, both evaluate to the literal string `"[object Object]"` — not a dynamic "any numeric key" matcher as apparently intended. The second key overwrites the first in the object literal, so the effective schema is just `{ access_token: z.string(), "[object Object]": z.unknown().optional() }`. Because `z.object()` strips unrecognized keys by default, `refreshTokenResponse.data` will only ever contain `access_token` (plus the dead `"[object Object]"` key) — all other fields (`expiry_date`, `refresh_token`, `instance_url`, etc.) are dropped. This directly feeds credential persistence: `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:90-96` does `parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema)` and saves the result to `prisma.credential.update`. With credential sync enabled this will corrupt/erase calendar credentials (losing `expiry_date`), silently breaking token refresh for every app that uses this helper.
